newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: AHOLD TO BUY 50 PCT OF BRAZILIAN CHAIN.
newsitem.headline: AHOLD TO BUY 50 PCT OF BRAZILIAN CHAIN.

text.p: Retail group Koninklijke Ahold said on Monday it had signed a letter of intent to buy a 50 percent stake in Brazilian supermarket chain Bompreco.
Bompreco is the fourth largest food retailer in Brazil and is market leader in the northeast of the country with 1995 consolidated annual sales of about $1.4 billion, Ahold said.
It said the acquisition would be financed from its available funds but gave no further financial details of the transaction.
"The investment for Ahold is anticipated to be non-dilutive to earnings per share in the first year and is expected to be earnings per share enhancing thereafter," it said.
Ahold added the goodwill connected with the transaction would be written off against equity capital and would therefore increase the company's gearing ratio.

Ahold said Bompreco had just concluded an international offering of preferred non-voting shares. Last week it sold nine million preferred shares to institutional investors in Brazil, the U.S. and Europe at a price of $8.25 each.
These shares are listed on the Brazilian Stock Exchanges and the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.

Ahold said it and Bompreco planned considerable expansion in the north and northeast of Brazil in the coming years. The Brazilian company currently operates seven hypermarkets, 29 supermarkets, 11 minimarkets and three department stores which will be remodeled into hypermarkets.
Ahold said it would contribute its know-how on retail technology, distribution, logistics and store operations to the joint venture.

"Once established, the new joint venture plans to aggressively further develop food retail operations in northeast Brazil by optimising the existing activities, opening new hypermarkets and large format supermarkets and acquiring other supermarket chains," the Dutch group added.
Ahold has annual sales of about $24 billion in the U.S., the Netherlands and other European countries. Recently it launched operations in Asia through a number of joint ventures.
